- When sentiment turns sharply positive (e.g., +1.67 or higher) followed by a spike in news volume, model tends to overreact and overshoot true price — reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- If sentiment shows strong negative momentum (e.g., -0.67+ change) and news volume drops, model underreacts — adjust forecast upward by 3–7% to avoid mean reversion bias.
- Model consistently underestimates true price when sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (0.00–0.67) — add 2–5% to forecast in such regimes.
- Overshoots after sentiment spikes are common in 30-day horizon — apply a 1–3 day lag correction: subtract 1–2% from forecast 2–3 days after spike.
- When sentiment change is flat (0.00) and news volume is low, model tends to drift — apply a 1–2% downward bias to prevent overconfidence in flat periods.
- If true outcome exceeds model by >3% for 3 consecutive days, model is underestimating — increase forecast by 1–3% for next 3 days unless sentiment shifts.
- Sentiment change >0.67 with news volume >3.0 implies upward momentum — model often misses it — add 1–2% to forecast if sentiment change >0.67 and news volume >2.5.
